question: Should I take a rest day tomorrow?

answer.summary: Rova can't tell you whether to rest from wearable data, so that call is yours. Here is what your training and recovery numbers show: your last 7 days sit within your usual range.

observed.text: Training load averaged 54.0 over the last 7 days, within your usual range of 33.5 to 69.9. Training duration averaged 58.3 min, within your usual range of 35.5 to 79.7 min.

Training load was above your usual range every day, peaking at 91 on Aug 18, with durations of 87 to 110 min. Sleep duration, sleep score and HRV were below your usual range on those days, while resting heart rate, temperature deviation and sleeping respiration were above it.
Training load was low on both days (20 on Aug 22, 28 on Aug 23), and sleep duration was above your usual range (7.8 h and 8.0 h).
On Aug 30, training load was 53.0 for 61 min, sleep was 7.1 h, HRV 51 ms and resting heart rate 54 bpm, all within your usual ranges.

interpretation: The Aug 16 – Aug 20 stretch shows heavy training and lower recovery numbers moving together, though the data can't show why.
Your last week looks similar to your own usual pattern, which may mean nothing stands out in these measures right now.
insufficientData: The file ends on Aug 30, so there is no data for the days since, including today or tomorrow. These measures also can't show how you feel, so they can't settle whether to rest.
answer.boundary: Rova can't tell whether you're unwell or diagnose anything from wearable data. If you're concerned about how you feel, a healthcare professional is the right person to ask.
answer.basis: Training load, training duration, sleep duration, sleep score, HRV, resting heart rate, temperature deviation and sleeping respiration, Aug 1 – Aug 30

question: Did hard training cause my bad sleep?

answer.summary: Rova can't say that hard training caused your poor sleep; the data can only show that they changed on the same days. Between Aug 16 and Aug 20, heavy training and your lowest sleep of the month coincided.

observed.text: Training load was above your usual range (33.5 to 69.9) on all five days: 72, 84, 91, 88 and 76. Training duration was also above usual, peaking at 110 min on Aug 18.
Sleep duration was below your usual range (6.65 h to 7.78 h) on each of these days, from 6.4 h down to 5.8 h on Aug 19.
Sleep score was also below your usual range (76.5 to 91.2), with a low of 67 on Aug 19.
Once training load dropped to 35 on Aug 21 and 20 on Aug 22, sleep duration returned to 7.4 h and 7.8 h, and sleep score to 84 and 88.

knowledge.title: Sleep score is your tracker's own measure
knowledge.text: Sleep score is your tracker's own calculation with no universal scale, so it is best compared with your own nights.

interpretation: The shorter, lower-scoring sleep may have been linked to the heavy training block, but the data can't show which affected which, or whether something else was going on.
Sleep recovering as training eased could fit that pattern, though it doesn't confirm a reason.
insufficientData: The data can't show why sleep dropped. It doesn't record other things that might have been happening on those days, so cause and effect can't be separated from this file.
answer.basis: Sleep duration, sleep score, training load and training duration, Aug 1 – Aug 30, compared with your own usual ranges
